source_review.notes: Reviewed the primary Michael-Scott PODC paper and expanded JPDC account, Herlihy-Wing linearizability, Herlihy progress theory, Michael hazard pointers, and current official Oracle Java 26, ISO C++ draft, and Rust atomic documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Claims about the original tail bound and read-before-head-CAS are attributed to the original algorithm; current library semantics are not treated as identical implementation evidence.

evidence: Checked abstract FIFO sequence, reachable chain, dummy exclusion, immutable successor relation, head/tail roles, and CAS notation.
Checked enqueue, nonempty dequeue, and empty linearization points plus private, live, dummy, retired, and reclaimable lifecycle states.
Checked progress, publication, identity, lifetime, capacity, and empirical variables remain distinct and scoped.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation maps the payload projection after Head to the abstract FIFO and never treats Tail as the membership boundary.

evidence: Recomputed bounded schedule: two link successes, two head successes, and two tail advances produce enqueue A,B and dequeue A,B.
Recomputed final Head=Tail=2, node 2 as the sole dummy, null successor, empty true, and one-node acyclic reachable chain.
Checked the capacity counterexample: two producers observing occupancy 99 against capacity 100 can both publish without atomic reservation.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No throughput, latency, memory-order, reclamation, or contention result is fabricated from the finite counts.

evidence: Verified each successful null-to-node link appends exactly one private node at the unique terminal link and permanently orders enqueues.
Verified each successful Head-to-successor CAS removes exactly the oldest payload and transfers the successor into the dummy role.
Verified Head equal Tail with null successor is empty, while a nonnull successor denotes one-link Tail lag and requires help/retry.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The FIFO and progress arguments are conditional on atomicity, safe publication, protected lifetime, no harmful ABA, and the original algorithm's tail invariant.

evidence: Reviewed empty, singleton, lagging Tail, enqueue-enqueue, dequeue-dequeue, enqueue-dequeue, invalid snapshots, stalled participants, and weak/spurious CAS.
Reviewed relaxed publication, unsafe value-read placement, immediate free, ABA/tag wrap, hazard announcement race, epoch stall, allocator failure, and garbage-collection assumptions.
Reviewed exact capacity, backpressure, lost wakeup, cancellation before/after point, close/drain/destruction, size/iteration, overload, NUMA, and retained memory.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial coverage includes both representation races and end-to-end operational/lifecycle failure boundaries.

evidence: The executable model permits link only at null, advances Tail only along an observed successor, and advances Head only to its immediate successor.
Exact assertions check the two deliberate lag states, FIFO return order, success/help counts, final head/tail/dummy identity, emptiness, and acyclicity.
Chapter invariants cover connected live chain, dummy role, payload projection, immutable links, operation points, bounded Tail lag, publication, lifetime, and ABA.
invariant_checking.notes: Unique integer node IDs and indivisible methods intentionally avoid ABA, reclamation, runtime atomic, and arbitrary-schedule concerns.

evidence: Reviewed initialization, enqueue validation/link/help, dequeue empty/help/head cases, and the distinction between abstract points and auxiliary Tail moves.
Reviewed connected-chain and FIFO induction, dummy-role transfer, consistent observations, original one-link Tail bound, publication, and lock-free system progress.
Reviewed proof dependencies for reclamation, ABA, exact capacity, blocking waits, cancellation, close, destruction, observation APIs, and all exercise solutions.
proof_review.notes: The proof does not silently extend the lock-free core to allocation, reclamation, notification, bounded admission, or lifecycle operations.

evidence: Successful link/head CAS and qualifying empty observation are explicitly labeled as candidate points under stated assumptions.
The lock-free argument is scoped to system progress for the abstract strong-CAS core and disclaims wait-freedom, fairness, and bounded latency.
The finite model, source checking, history tests, memory tools, fault tests, and benchmarks are separated by evidence type.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No stress pass, absence of mutexes, tail repair, or benchmark result is generalized into universal safety or progress.

evidence: The standard-library-only Python schedule passed exact eleven-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It emits evidence=finite_michael_scott_schedule_model and reproduces two delayed Tail swings, helping, FIFO removals, and the final dummy state.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local links passed chapter validation.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real threads, atomics, memory visibility, arbitrary history, ABA/reclamation, progress, allocator, blocking, lifecycle, or performance experiment was run.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter derives the queue from sequential FIFO, separates link membership from lagging Tail navigation, establishes operation points and system progress, then exposes memory, lifetime, capacity, lifecycle, and evidence assumptions.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed publication/consumption paths, payload read timing, hazard/epoch/tag choices, allocation and retired-memory bounds, exact admission, lost wakeups, cancellation, close/drain/quiescence, observation limits, diagnostics, alternatives, and rollback criteria.

pedagogical_review.notes: The review sheet isolates the sentinel, points, lag, and caveats; the finite schedule makes helping concrete; ten examples span safety and production transfer; five progressive exercises have complete diagnostic and design answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/official-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, Michael, Scott, Herlihy, Wing, Oracle, ISO C++, Rust, concurrency, security, performance, reliability, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and finite model prove neither a concrete runtime queue, real threads/CAS, target memory orders, arbitrary histories, ABA prevention, safe reclamation, allocator progress, exact bounded capacity, blocking wakeups, close/destruction, fairness/starvation bounds, production throughput/latency/coherence/NUMA behavior, certification, nor deployment fitness.
